objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (19 November 2026) on PARENT-RULE-20261119-001's direction 1. PARENT-RULE showed backed pairs do not keep the states (242 static pairs) and that what protects reached stages must be the law's exact joins and counts; but only 85 small arrangements are self-grown. Grow every one of the 503,039 legal meet-once arrangements of at most 7 junctions by one and two complete rounds of the law (cheapest counts) and search the resulting stages, all of which meet once, for non-isomorphic pairs with isomorphic full bond-distance tables and other allowed states. Stop at such a pair, or none. Serves A97 and G1.
status: Complete 2026-11-19 (Successful; referee pending): yes. Grown one and two complete rounds from all 503,039 legal meet-once arrangements of at most 7 junctions, the census's law makes 67 groups (87 pairs) of non-isomorphic meet-once stages with isomorphic full bond-distance tables and other allowed states: 86 pairs carried from starts that already collide, 1 created from starts with different tables. MEET-ONCE's and PARENT-RULE's readings narrowed to the census's starts (Narrowing).
stop_rule: A reached meet-once pair with isomorphic full tables and other states, or none among the stages of rounds 1 and 2; referee hand-off; report.
title: Does the law, grown from every small arrangement, ever make a meet-once collision with other states?
